ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.90 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexempted detour kilometre units; keep the $1.19 metered waiting charge (RD-3(c) — RydeTAXI waiting units are chargeable) and the residual corridor/matching kilometres (RD-2). No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a RydeTAXI metered journey with one recorded off-route segment, which the trace confirms exists [F4][RD-1]. No exemption applies to it: no qualifying incident was recorded on the replaced stretch [F15][RD-4(a)], the PIE and CTE band-4 readings are expressly insufficient on their own [F13][F14][RD-4(b)], and the weather was fair [F16][RD-4].

I read the only two chat messages. The rider wrote “Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes” [F9] and the driver answered “Sure” [F10]. That is a request for an unnamed stop, accepted before the segment began at 17:37 [F4], so timing under RD-5 is satisfied but scope is not: an unnamed “a 7-Eleven on the way” is neither a general route choice nor a named road or area, and the driver’s own statement that he went to “the one I know” [F12] places the chosen store off the path. Under RD-3(a) the exemption requires the rider to have named a specific place and the car to have stopped there; she named none, so the extra kilometre units of the segment are not excused [RD-3][RD-5].

The stationary stop of 4 min 10 s [F2] sits inside the segment, and on RydeTAXI in-trip waiting is a metered waiting unit item [F6][F8], which RD-3(c) says is charged, not refunded; so the $1.19 waiting line stays and only the unmetred-excused kilometre units come back [RD-3][RD-2].

Amount: the segment’s extra distance is 4.89 km [F4] and the trip’s per-kilometre rate is the fare record’s distance fare ÷ distance km, $29.53 ÷ 20.94 km = $1.4102/km [F8]. 4.89 × $1.4102 = $6.8958, rounded to the cent = $6.90 [RD-2]. The billed excess of 5.47 km / $7.71 [F5] is not fully claimable: the 0.58 km gap between it and the segment is corridor and map-matching residue that RD-2 leaves untouched [RD-2].

No account flag: the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days [F18], so RD-6’s repetition condition is not met and the flag falls away [RD-6]. Safety screen done: the complaint and both chat messages are about a stop, a route and the meter — nothing threatening, harassing or dangerous [F9][F10][F12][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is complete: both messages timestamped [F11], GPS covers the segment and the stop [F4][F2], and the fare record gives the rate [F8].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's message [F9] asks for a 7-Eleven “on the way” without naming any place, and the driver only replied “Sure” [F10]; the driver then chose the store himself, as his own statement concedes [F12]. RD-5 consent here is neither a general route choice nor a specific named road or area, and the record places the stop away from the optimal path (up to 1268 m off) rather than on any agreed route [F4]; RD-3(a) does not exempt a stop whose place the rider never named. The segment's extra 4.89 km is therefore an unexempted detour under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Withdrawn by the rider and in any case defeated by the profile: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F18], so RD-6's repetition condition is not established and no account flag follows [RD-6].

The pre-segment timing of the request [F9] and acceptance [F10] is not disputed, but a timely unnamed stop request does not cover a 7.60 km corridor reaching 1268 m off the optimal route [F4]; RD-5 requires the agreement to cover the segment, and RD-3(a) requires a named place.

The driver's own reading admits the rider named no place [F9][F10]; under RD-3(a) an unnamed stop gives no excuse for the driver's choice of a far store [F12], so the segment's extra kilometres remain unexempted [F4].

The 4 min 10 s stationary period [F2] lies inside the unexempted segment [F4]; on RydeTAXI the metered waiting unit is chargeable under RD-3(c), so this does not reduce the distance refund of $6.90 [F8].
The $1.19 waiting line [F6][F8] is a metered waiting unit item, and RD-3(c) keeps metered in-trip waiting chargeable; it is therefore not refunded and does not offset the RD-2 distance refund.
The “about $36.75 optimal-route” counterfactual is not computed from any gps or fare fact; RD-2 refunds only unexempted extra_km, and the metered fare [F8] supports only the segment figure of $6.90.
